question: 1. What is the role of a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) inside Latent Diffusion Models like Stable Diffusion?

options.A: To compress high-resolution images into a lower-dimensional latent space where noise reduction occurs efficiently
options.B: To convert text prompts into one-hot frequency vectors
options.C: To align audio frequencies with character n-grams
options.D: To replace Transformer multi-head attention layers

explanation: In Latent Diffusion, a VAE encoder squeezes pixel-space images into a compressed latent space (e.g. 8x spatial compression) so that denoising steps run rapidly on consumer GPUs.

question: 2. How does text conditioning guide image generation in a Diffusion Model?

options.A: By concatenating text string lengths to image resolution dimensions
options.B: By passing text prompt embeddings from CLIP/T5 into Cross-Attention mechanisms inside the U-Net or Transformer backbone layers
options.C: By converting text into Laplace add-1 smoothing constants
options.D: By running SVD decomposition on prompt co-occurrence counts

explanation: Text conditioning uses cross-attention layers, where image feature maps act as Queries and text prompt embeddings (from CLIP or T5) act as Keys and Values to guide feature synthesis.

question: 3. What is Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) in text-to-image diffusion models?

options.A: A mechanism that balances adherence to the text prompt versus visual quality and diversity by combining conditional and unconditional score estimates
options.B: A classifier network that deletes low-resolution images
options.C: A rule-based grammar parser that removes profanity from text prompts
options.D: A algorithm that sets model temperature to zero

explanation: Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) pushes the generated sample towards the text prompt by extrapolating predictions between conditional (prompted) and unconditional (empty prompt) denoising steps.

question: 4. What role does the 'Random Seed' integer play in generative AI media creation?

options.A: It sets the initial Gaussian noise matrix state, allowing exact reproducibility of synthesized images, audio, or video across identical prompts and settings
options.B: It sets the maximum token length limit
options.C: It controls the learning rate during model backpropagation
options.D: It measures cosine distance between text vectors

explanation: Fixing the random seed initializes pseudo-random noise generators to the exact same starting tensor, ensuring deterministic reproducibility of generative outputs.

question: 5. What architectural innovation enables single-step or few-step real-time diffusion models (e.g., SD-Turbo, ADD, LCM)?

options.A: Model distillation techniques (Adversarial Diffusion Distillation / Consistency Models) that compress 50 multi-step denoising iterations into 1-4 fast steps
options.B: Removing cross-attention layers completely
options.C: Using one-hot vectors for image pixel rendering
options.D: Increasing image resolution by 100x

explanation: Real-time diffusion distillation (like ADD and Consistency Distillation) trains student networks to map noise to clean outputs in 1-4 steps, bypassing slow 50-step iterative sampling.

question: 6. How do generative audio architectures like Meta's MusicGen and EnCodec produce high-fidelity music and speech?

options.A: By tokenizing continuous audio signals into discrete neural audio codes using neural audio codecs (EnCodec) and modeling them autoregressively with Transformers
options.B: By converting audio directly into ASCII text strings
options.C: By running SVD decomposition on co-occurrence counts
options.D: By using rule-based MIDI synthesizers from the 1980s

explanation: MusicGen uses neural audio codecs (EnCodec) to quantize raw audio waveforms into discrete codebook tokens, which an autoregressive Transformer predicts conditioned on text embeddings.

question: 7. How do state-of-the-art video generation architectures like OpenAI Sora synthesize extended, photorealistic video clips?

options.A: By applying Spatiotemporal Diffusion Transformers (DiT) operating on 3D spacetime video latent patches
options.B: By stitching static 2D JPEG images together sequentially with no temporal modeling
options.C: By applying N-gram Markov chains on optical flow vectors
options.D: By using TF-IDF document weights on video metadata text

explanation: Sora and modern video models decompose video into 3D spacetime latent patches and process them using Diffusion Transformers (DiT) to maintain temporal consistency and spatial geometry.

question: 8. What is Google SynthID and how does it address AI media provenance and deepfake detection?

options.A: An imperceptible digital watermark embedded directly into generated image pixels or audio waveforms during synthesis that survives cropping, compression, and editing
options.B: A public registry requiring human creators to upload passport photos
options.C: A text filter that blocks prompt execution
options.D: A database storing every generated image file name

explanation: SynthID embeds subtle, imperceptible watermarks directly into image latent representations or audio frequency spectra during generation, enabling reliable detection even after transformations.

question: 9. What is the purpose of the C2PA (Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity) technical standard in generative media governance?

options.A: Attaching cryptographically verifiable manifest metadata to media files recording origin history, AI tool usage, and edit logs
options.B: Compressing MP4 video files into ZIP archives
options.C: Enforcing maximum resolution limits on image generation
options.D: Calculating term frequency-inverse document frequency

explanation: C2PA provides an open technical specification for embedding tamper-evident cryptographic metadata manifests into digital media to verify content origin and AI generation lineage.

question: 10. In text-to-image synthesis, what happens if the Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) scale parameter is set excessively high (e.g., CFG = 30)?

options.A: The generated image suffers from severe over-saturation, harsh contrast clipping, and unnatural visual artifacts
options.B: The image becomes completely blur-free and photorealistic
options.C: The model generates a blank white canvas
options.D: The random seed is automatically reset to zero

explanation: Setting CFG too high over-constrains the sampling trajectory, causing extreme color saturation, over-sharpening artifacts, and loss of natural texture.

question: 11. How does CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining) align textual descriptions with visual images in a shared vector embedding space?

options.A: By jointly training a Text Encoder and Image Encoder on 400M image-text pairs using a contrastive loss that maximizes cosine similarity for correct pairs
options.B: By converting text into one-hot vectors and images into grayscale matrices
options.C: By running SVD decomposition on co-occurrence matrices
options.D: By using rule-based feature extraction for edge detection

explanation: CLIP uses contrastive learning across dual encoders (text and image) to map matching image-caption pairs to high cosine similarity in a shared multimodal embedding space.

question: 12. What is the fundamental difference between a GAN Generator and a Diffusion Model Denoising U-Net during image creation?

options.A: A GAN Generator maps a random noise vector to a complete image in a single forward pass; a Diffusion U-Net iteratively removes noise over multiple sequential steps
options.B: A GAN Generator uses attention layers, while Diffusion models do not
options.C: Diffusion models only produce black-and-white images
options.D: A GAN Generator relies on text-conditioned cross attention

explanation: GAN Generators synthesize full output images in one single feedforward pass, whereas Diffusion models construct images iteratively through t time steps of score-based noise prediction.

question: 13. What is an 'Image-to-Image' (Img2Img) diffusion pipeline?

options.A: A pipeline that takes an existing input image, adds noise up to step t, and denoises it conditioned on a text prompt to modify style or content while preserving structure
options.B: A method for converting JPEG files into PNG format
options.C: A database query that matches duplicate image files
options.D: A loss function measuring pixel squared error

explanation: Img2Img partially corrupts a user-provided base image with Gaussian noise, then applies text-guided denoising to transform visual style while maintaining underlying layout geometry.

question: 14. How does Inpainting differ from Outpainting in generative image editing tools?

options.A: Inpainting generates content inside a user-masked region of an image; Outpainting extends the image canvas beyond its original borders while maintaining context
options.B: Inpainting edits audio tracks; Outpainting edits text files
options.C: Inpainting increases resolution; Outpainting converts images to 3D meshes
options.D: Inpainting uses GANs; Outpainting uses static N-grams

explanation: Inpainting fills or modifies specific masked interior regions of an image, whereas Outpainting expands visual content outward beyond the original frame boundaries.

question: 15. Why are Multimodal LLMs (e.g., GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5, LLaVA) replacing separate pipeline systems for vision and language tasks?

options.A: Because natively processing text, audio, and visual tokens within unified Transformer architectures allows joint cross-modal reasoning and lower latency
options.B: Because single-modal models can no longer execute text tokenization
options.C: Because multimodal models require zero training compute memory
options.D: Because image pixels can be converted directly into one-hot encodings

explanation: Native multimodal models project images, video, audio, and text into a shared token space within a unified Transformer model, enabling direct cross-modal reasoning without modular handoffs.

question: 16. In text-to-image diffusion pipelines, what occurs if the Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) scale is set too low (e.g., CFG = 1.0)?

options.A: The generated image exhibits high visual diversity but ignores detailed prompt instructions and constraints
options.B: The generated image exhibits over-saturated contrast artifacts
options.C: The model fails to initialize Gaussian noise tensors
options.D: The output resolution drops to 16x16 pixels

explanation: At low CFG scales (near 1.0), the model relies mostly on unconditional generation, yielding diverse but loosely prompt-adherent outputs.

question: 17. What is CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training) and how does it bridge text prompts with visual synthesis?

options.A: CLIP jointly trains an Image Encoder and Text Encoder on hundreds of millions of image-caption pairs using contrastive loss, projecting text and images into a shared embedding space
options.B: CLIP converts image pixels directly into ASCII character strings
options.C: CLIP calculates term frequency inverse document weights across image metadata
options.D: CLIP is an audio codec for speech compression

explanation: CLIP creates a shared multimodal embedding space where text description vectors and image feature vectors can be compared directly using cosine similarity.

question: 18. What structural capabilities does ControlNet add to pretrained text-to-image diffusion models?

options.A: ControlNet attaches conditional spatial adapters to diffusion models, enforcing explicit geometric control using depth maps, Canny edges, segmentation masks, or pose skeletons
options.B: ControlNet accelerates generation speeds by 100x without GPU memory
options.C: ControlNet converts diffusion models into autoregressive language decoders
options.D: ControlNet removes text conditioning entirely

explanation: ControlNet locks original diffusion weights and trains lightweight trainable copies to condition output generation on precise spatial controls like edge maps, depth, or human poses.

question: 19. Why is Latent Diffusion (e.g., Stable Diffusion) drastically more efficient than Pixel-Space Diffusion (e.g., Imagen or early DDPM)?

options.A: Latent Diffusion performs noise addition and reverse score estimation in a compressed latent space (e.g., 64x lower spatial dimension), reducing GPU compute memory requirements dramatically
options.B: Pixel-space diffusion cannot process color images
options.C: Latent diffusion eliminates the need for score functions
options.D: Pixel-space diffusion requires custom TPU chips

explanation: By running diffusion steps in a compressed VAE latent representation rather than full pixel space, Latent Diffusion slashes computational complexity and memory usage by orders of magnitude.

question: 20. What key advantage does a Diffusion Transformer (DiT) architecture offer over traditional U-Net backbones for generative media (such as OpenAI Sora and SD3)?

options.A: DiT replaces convolutional U-Net layers with Transformer blocks operating on spacetime latent patches, enabling predictable compute parameter scaling laws and superior long-context video modeling
options.B: DiT eliminates positional encodings from video generation
options.C: DiT converts latent tokens into one-hot vectors
options.D: DiT reduces video framerates to 1 fps

explanation: Diffusion Transformers (DiT) treat image/video latents as sequence patches, unlocking Transformer parameter scaling laws, superior spatial-temporal modeling, and efficient multi-modal attention.

question: 1. What is the fundamental architecture and primary advantage of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) over pure LLM fine-tuning for enterprise knowledge bases?

options.A: RAG modifies the underlying transformer attention weights, eliminating the need for context windows
options.B: RAG retrieves relevant external text chunks at query time and pastes them into the prompt, allowing models to cite sources without costly retraining
options.C: RAG replaces vector embeddings with one-hot encoding matrices to prevent hallucinations
options.D: RAG retrains the model body on thousands of GPUs every time a new document is added

explanation: RAG operates by indexing documents into vector chunks, retrieving top matches per query, and inserting them into the context window. This grounds the answer in external truth without modifying model parameters.

question: 2. In the 3-step RAG pipeline (Indexing, Retrieval, Generation), when is the 'Indexing' phase executed?

options.A: Dynamically during every user query in real time
options.B: Once upfront before queries arrive (and updated whenever underlying documents change), by chunking text and storing vector embeddings in a database
options.C: After the LLM generates its response to verify factual accuracy
options.D: During the pretraining phase of foundation models like GPT-4

explanation: Indexing is an offline pre-processing step performed once (or upon document updates) where documents are split into chunks, transformed into embedding vectors, and saved in a vector database.

question: 3. [Scenario] An e-commerce company notices their customer support RAG system generates incorrect return policy advice when a user asks about 'money back', because the policy document uses the word 'refund'. How does semantic vector search resolve this issue compared to keyword search?

options.A: Semantic search forces the user to retype their query using exact keyword matches
options.B: Semantic search converts words/chunks into dense vector embeddings where 'money back' and 'refund' sit close together in vector space, finding the chunk regardless of exact phrasing
options.C: Semantic search retrains the LLM tokenizer on e-commerce dictionary definitions
options.D: Semantic search uses Bigram frequency tables to eliminate non-matching tokens

explanation: Unlike keyword search (TF-IDF) which requires exact term matches, semantic vector search measures distance in high-dimensional embedding space (e.g. via cosine similarity), recognizing that 'money back' and 'refund' share semantic meaning.

question: 4. [Scenario] A law firm feeds a 100-page contract into a long-context LLM, but the model fails to reference a critical indemnity clause located on page 45. What known phenomenon explains this failure?

options.A: Vanishing gradient during backpropagation
options.B: The 'Lost in the Middle' effect, where LLMs recall information at the beginning or end of long context prompts much better than information placed in the middle
options.C: Mode collapse in autoregressive decoders
options.D: Subword tokenization collapse

explanation: Research (Liu et al., 2023) proves that language models exhibit a U-shaped performance curve in long context windows: retrieval accuracy is highest for facts near the top or bottom of the prompt, and drops significantly for facts buried in the middle.

question: 5. How does a Chunking strategy impact RAG performance when processing structured financial tables or complex multi-column documents?

options.A: Chunking has zero impact on retrieval accuracy as long as the vector database is large
options.B: Splitting text too aggressively can inadvertently separate table headers from numerical rows, destroying context and leading to inaccurate retrieved chunks
options.C: Chunking automatically converts table cells into one-hot encoded integers
options.D: Chunking increases the parameter count of the generator LLM

explanation: If document chunking boundaries cut through a table, the header row and numerical data rows end up in separate chunks, causing semantic vector search to lose crucial row-header associations.

question: 6. What is the role of an 'LLM-as-a-Judge' or Faithfulness Evaluator (e.g., Vectara HHEM or secondary auditor model) in an enterprise RAG system?

options.A: It converts text inputs into speech audio files for accessibility
options.B: It evaluates generated answers sentence-by-sentence against retrieved source chunks to verify whether every claim is explicitly supported by the text
options.C: It fine-tunes the base model's self-attention projection matrices
options.D: It generates synthetic images to accompany text responses

explanation: Faithfulness evaluators or judge models automatically audit generated answers against retrieved context chunks, flagging unsupported claims or hallucinations before outputs are shown to users.

question: 7. [Scenario] An enterprise RAG system frequently retrieves irrelevant document chunks when users ask questions on out-of-scope topics (e.g., asking a healthcare bot about mortgage rates). What mitigation strategy should be implemented in the retrieval step?

options.A: Increase model Temperature to 1.5 to encourage creative guesses
options.B: Set a minimum similarity score threshold (e.g. cosine score < 0.4); if no retrieved chunk meets the threshold, prompt the model to answer 'Information not found in sources'
options.C: Disable vector embeddings and use random sampling
options.D: Switch from a Decoder model to an Encoder-only model

explanation: Establishing a similarity threshold prevents low-scoring irrelevant chunks from polluting the prompt context, allowing the system to safely return an out-of-scope refusal.

question: 8. What is 'Hybrid Search' in modern enterprise retrieval architectures?

options.A: Combining image diffusion with text-to-speech generation
options.B: Combining sparse keyword search (e.g., BM25/TF-IDF) with dense vector semantic search to catch both exact technical product codes/names and conceptual meaning
options.C: Combining supervised fine-tuning with reinforcement learning
options.D: Combining one-hot vectors with character n-grams

explanation: Hybrid search merges keyword search (excellent for rare part numbers, acronyms, and proper nouns) with dense vector search (excellent for conceptual meaning and synonyms).

question: 9. What is the purpose of a 'Reranker' model (e.g., Cross-Encoder) placed after initial vector retrieval in an Advanced RAG pipeline?

options.A: To compress the context window into 10 tokens
options.B: To perform a secondary, highly precise re-scoring of the top candidate chunks and place the single most relevant chunk at the very beginning of the prompt to avoid 'Lost in the Middle' errors
options.C: To update model weights during user sessions
options.D: To convert markdown text into PDF formatting

explanation: A Reranker uses a cross-encoder to thoroughly re-evaluate the top retrieved chunks against the query, ensuring the highest quality chunk is positioned at the top of the prompt.

question: 10. In a grounded prompt for RAG, why is it critical to include explicit citation instructions (e.g., 'Cite the chunk number in brackets like [1]')?

options.A: It speeds up GPU matrix multiplication during inference
options.B: It enables human auditability, allowing staff to verify generated claims directly against source documents and catch subtle errors
options.C: It decreases context window memory usage
options.D: It replaces the need for vector embeddings

explanation: Grounding prompts with bracketed citations enforce traceability, allowing human reviewers or auditing scripts to verify that generated figures or claims match the cited source.

question: 11. [Scenario] A bank wants to deploy an internal chatbot to help staff query 50,000 PDF compliance manuals. The compliance team mandates zero tolerance for made-up policies, strict source traceability, and instant updates whenever a regulation changes. Which technology approach best satisfies these constraints?

options.A: Full pretraining of a new 70B parameter base model from scratch
options.B: Fine-tuning an existing base LLM on all compliance PDFs
options.C: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) paired with a Vector Database, similarity thresholds, and explicit citation prompts
options.D: Few-shot prompting without external retrieval or documents

explanation: RAG provides grounded answers with source citations and instantaneous index updates when policies change, whereas pretraining/fine-tuning are expensive, lack source citations, and hallucinate.

question: 12. What vector metric is most commonly used in vector databases (e.g., Pinecone, Qdrant, Chroma) to calculate similarity between query embeddings and document chunk embeddings?

options.A: Hamming distance on one-hot arrays
options.B: Cosine Similarity (or normalized Dot Product), measuring the angle between two dense embedding vectors in high-dimensional space
options.C: Add-1 Laplace smoothing ratio
options.D: Perplexity score

explanation: Cosine similarity calculates the cosine of the angle between two embedding vectors in multidimensional space; values closer to 1.0 indicate high semantic similarity.

question: 13. What is 'Naive RAG' compared to 'Advanced RAG'?

options.A: Naive RAG uses RNNs; Advanced RAG uses linear regression
options.B: Naive RAG directly pastes top vector matches into the prompt, whereas Advanced RAG incorporates pre-retrieval optimization (query expansion/rewriting), post-retrieval optimization (reranking/filtering), and modular index structures
options.C: Naive RAG operates without a language model
options.D: Naive RAG requires human annotators to write responses manually

explanation: Naive RAG simply retrieves and pastes text. Advanced RAG optimizes query generation, filters/reranks chunks, and manages index structures to maximize factual retrieval accuracy.

question: 14. [Scenario] A medical diagnostic assistant built with RAG is tested on 1,000 patient queries. In 8% of cases, the system returns an answer containing an accurate medical fact, but the cited source document contains no mention of that fact. How is this error classified in RAG evaluation?

options.A: High retrieval precision
options.B: Unfaithful generation / Extrapolated hallucination (answering from model parametric memory rather than grounded source context)
options.C: Context window overflow
options.D: Temperature zero clipping

explanation: When an LLM pulls facts from its internal pretrained parametric memory rather than relying strictly on the retrieved context, it breaks grounding (unfaithful generation), creating compliance risks.

question: 15. What is the role of 'Document Pre-processing & Parsing' prior to vector embedding in a RAG pipeline?

options.A: Compressing text into single-character tokens
options.B: Extracting clean text, headers, metadata, and visual structure from raw PDFs, HTML, or DOCX files so chunking algorithms can split text along logical boundaries
options.C: Calculating perplexity scores across internet corpora
options.D: Fine-tuning transformer decoder projection layers

explanation: Parsing converts unstructured files (PDFs, slides, web pages) into clean structured text with metadata, ensuring chunks preserve logical context like section headings and page numbers.

question: 16. In RAG system evaluation, what are the two core metrics known as 'RAG Triad' or 'Grounding Metrics'?

options.A: Perplexity and BLEU score
options.B: Context Relevance (did retrieval find the right chunks?) and Groundedness / Faithfulness (is the generated response strictly backed by those chunks?)
options.C: One-hot sparsity and SVD rank
options.D: Temperature and Top-P threshold

explanation: Evaluating RAG requires checking Context Relevance (retrieval quality) and Groundedness/Faithfulness (generation quality relative to retrieved context).

question: 17. [Scenario] A corporate knowledge assistant needs to respect strict user permission roles (e.g. HR staff can view salary documents, but general staff cannot). At what stage of the RAG pipeline should access control filtering be enforced?

options.A: In the prompt post-processing step after the LLM generates the text
options.B: During the Retrieval / Vector Search stage (metadata filtering), ensuring unauthorized document chunks are never retrieved or injected into the prompt context
options.C: During pretraining of the base foundation model
options.D: By setting model Temperature to 0.0

explanation: Access control must be enforced at retrieval time using vector metadata filtering so unauthorized text chunks are never exposed to the LLM context window.

question: 18. How does 'Query Rewriting / Expansion' improve retrieval performance in Advanced RAG?

options.A: It translates the query into binary machine code
options.B: It uses an LLM to reformulate vague user queries, add context, or break complex questions into multiple sub-queries before searching the vector index
options.C: It removes all vowels from the query string
options.D: It replaces semantic vector search with one-hot matrix multiplication

explanation: Query expansion/rewriting transforms conversational or ambiguous user prompts into clean, search-optimized queries that match the vocabulary of indexed document chunks.

question: 19. What is 'Modular RAG'?

options.A: A RAG system built without neural networks
options.B: An architecture that integrates specialized interchangeable modules like routing, search, memory, knowledge graph traversal, and iterative multi-step retrieval loops
options.C: A model fine-tuned on single-word dictionary terms
options.D: A database storing raw audio waveforms

explanation: Modular RAG expands beyond linear search-and-generate pipelines by incorporating dynamic routing, knowledge graph reasoning, and iterative feedback loops.

question: 20. Why is a Continuous Test Set / Regression Evaluation Loop essential for maintaining production RAG systems?

options.A: Because vector database indexes degrade automatically every 24 hours
options.B: To systematically re-evaluate system accuracy against a fixed suite of golden Q&A test cases whenever prompt templates, chunking parameters, or embedding models are updated
options.C: To train the generator LLM from scratch on daily user chat logs
options.D: To reset temperature and top-k hyperparameters

explanation: Running automated regression tests against a golden benchmark dataset ensures that changes to chunk sizes, prompts, or embedding models do not introduce accuracy regressions.
